articles.body: A single M2 Max Mac Studio can serve 8‑token‑per‑second Llama‑2‑7B inference, yet most developers leave that compute idle overnight. ## Inventory and Network Topology Start by enumerating every Apple Silicon machine on the LAN. arp-scan --localnet | grep -i apple returns MAC addresses and hostnames. In a typical lab you might see two M2 Max units (38‑core GPU, 400 GB/s bandwidth), one M3 Ultra (80‑core GPU, 800 GB/s), and one M1 Pro (16‑core GPU). Record each host, its GPU core count, and unified memory size in a YAML inventory. Then run exo cluster init --config inventory.yaml on every node so Exo can build a peer‑to‑peer mesh over mDNS. Action: Create an inventory YAML and run exo cluster init --config inventory.yaml on each Mac to join the cluster.

articles.body: A delivery moves from Tuesday to Thursday. The person who moved it knows. The customer who planned their week around Tuesday does not. Neither does the colleague who promised to be there to receive it. Nothing went wrong in the work itself. The failure was a message that did not get sent. Small changes cause big annoyance Most of the complaints a business gets are not about the change. A delay is usually forgivable. What people remember is finding out late, or finding out from someone else. Inside the team it works the same way. A price changes, a person goes on leave, a supplier switches. Each of those means someone else has to adjust, and each depends on someone remembering who that someone is.

articles.title: Multi-tenant SaaS with branch-level RBAC in Next.js + Node: a practical architecture
articles.excerpt: Tenant scoping that fails closed, permissions that know about branches, and the tests that keep both honest. Key takeaways Resolve the tenant from the session, never from the request. A URL slug or he…
articles.body: Tenant scoping that fails closed, permissions that know about branches, and the tests that keep both honest. Key takeaways Resolve the tenant from the session, never from the request. A URL slug or header can select which of your memberships to use, but the server must verify that membership. Next.js middleware is a gate, not a guard. Use it for redirects and cheap checks; do real authorization next to the data, in your Node API or server code. Every Server Action and Route Handler is a public endpoint. Authorize inside each one, every time. Make the database refuse cross-tenant reads. PostgreSQL row-level security with a transaction-local setting means a forgotten filter returns nothing instead of someone else's data. Permissions are (action, scope) , not role names.

articles.title: Selling downloads across borders: a field guide for buyers who are never in your time zone
articles.excerpt: A domestic sale is forgiving. If delivery hiccups, you are probably awake, probably online, and able to fix it before the buyer loses patience. An overseas sale removes every one of those safety nets.…
articles.body: A domestic sale is forgiving. If delivery hiccups, you are probably awake, probably online, and able to fix it before the buyer loses patience. An overseas sale removes every one of those safety nets. The buyer checks out while you sleep, pays in a currency you have never held, downloads over a connection you would complain about, and sends their one support message eight hours before you wake up. Nothing about the product changes — everything about the delivery has to work unattended. This is a field guide organised by the moments where international sales actually break, not by platform features. Most of it costs nothing but decisions made in advance. Moment one: the purchase happens while you sleep The defining fact of global buyers is that your shop's busiest moment may be your 3 a.m.

articles.title: Express.js Transactional Email Service Wrapper: 5 Retry and Logging Layers
articles.excerpt: A welcome email should leave the request path quickly, but accepting a job is not the same as delivering a message. The reliable design is a small Node.js service wrapper around a direct email API, ba…
articles.body: A welcome email should leave the request path quickly, but accepting a job is not the same as delivering a message. The reliable design is a small Node.js service wrapper around a direct email API, backed by a durable queue, a suppression check, stored provider message IDs, and polling for delivery events. Do not build this around SMTP when the chosen capability is API-only. The API boundary gives the application enough structure to decide what may be retried and what must be suppressed. TL;DR: enqueue one idempotent welcome-email job, check suppression immediately before each send, persist the returned message ID, and poll message events into a local delivery record. A bounce should update suppression before another queued job can target that address.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 13, 1773: Astronomer Charles Messier discovers the Whirlpool Galaxy before we ever knew it was a galaxy
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 13, 1773, a French astronomer named Charles Messier discovered the "Whirlpool Galaxy," also known as Messier 51, or M51. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 13, 1773, a French astronomer named Charles Messier discovered the " Whirlpool Galaxy , " also known as Messier 51, or M51. Charles Messier was scanning the sky for objects that could confuse comet hunters when he catalogued the galaxy as M51. However, Messier wasn't able to see the spiral structure, and he didn't identify it as a galaxy. Seventy-two years later, another astronomer named William Parsons saw the whirlpool shape, but he thought it was a spiral nebula. Eventually, Edwin Hubble found out that M51 and other features like it were actually galaxies. Spiral galaxy M51 (NGC 5194), The Whirlpool Galaxy, displays its long arms which consist of stars and gas laced with dust arranged in long lanes, in this view from the Hubble Space Telescope.

articles.body: NEW YORK — Set your phasers to back-to-school, space fans. Star Trek is going back to Starfleet Academy for season 2, and we finally have a release date. The sophomore season of " Star Trek: Starfleet Academy " will warp back to the small screen in March 2027 when the limited series returns for its final season on Paramount+ . The series, which follows a class of cadets balancing Starfleet classes, space adventures (and yes, some love) in the 32nd century, will return with its full cast and even add new faces, showrunners announced at a panel at New York Comic Con 2026 on Saturday (Oct. 10). articles.body: Nostalgia is a hell of a thing, especially when it comes to sci-fi. For "Star Trek" fans wanting to mark the franchise's 60th anniversary this year, a geeky pilgrimage to upstate New York should be on the cards. Why? Because alongside the splendid autumnal colors, they can steer over to Ticonderoga to behold the newly installed Galileo shuttlecraft. After a complete two-year restoration project in 2012 headed up by superfan and collector Adam Schneider, this iconic fictional spacecraft, seen by millions in seven episodes over three seasons of "Star Trek: The Original Series," was recently relocated from its former home at the Johnson Space Center Museum in Houston, Texas.

articles.title: Earth's poles shifted surprisingly fast during the age of dinosaurs, ancient sea levels reveal
articles.excerpt: The location of Earth's geographic poles has changed several times over the past 320 million years in a process known as true polar wander.
articles.body: The location of Earth's geographic poles has changed several times over the past 320 million years in a process known as true polar wander, according to measurements of ancient flooding brought about by sea level changes resulting from our planet's crust shifting relative to Earth's spin axis. Such a shift can affect climate, both on local scales and globally, as regions that were by the poles find themselves moving down to lower latitudes and vice versa. This can then affect atmospheric circulation patterns, which affect climate across the world. The changes would have affected the environments in which life developed and evolved, from the age of the dinosaurs through to some of our oldest primate ancestors.

articles.title: SpaceX rocket launch creates incredible 'space jellyfish' visible throughout US East Coast (photos)
articles.excerpt: The SpaceX cargo launch to the International Space Station on Tuesday morning (Oct. 13) created a dazzling display seen up and down the US East Coast.
articles.body: Rockets are launching to space on a near-daily basis these days, but short of livestreaming a liftoff from the comfort of your Wi-Fi router, relatively few spectators are in the right place and time to see one with their own eyes. That wasn't the case Tuesday morning (Oct. 13), when SpaceX launched the CRS-35 mission for NASA . A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Pad 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida at 6:35 a.m. EDT (1035 GMT), carrying a cargo variant of SpaceX's Dragon spacecraft on the company's 35th commercial resupply mission to the International Space Station (ISS). Following the northward path of the space station's orbit at the time, the rocket flew a trajectory along the United States' East Coast.
